snippet.title: Queen Elizabeth had an unfaithful husband
snippet.description: Queen Elizabeth had an unfaithful husband. Prince Philip was a real beauty: a stately, tall, blue-eyed blond naval officer from a noble family. At the dawn of their married life, the couple often lived apart, which gave rise to speculation of imminent divorce and possible infidelity. Philip spent time in private men's clubs of dubious character, and although British newspapers have never been able to put on the front page of the sensation devoted to the leisure consort, the list of his alleged mistresses could well take a whole front page. At one time it included such personalities as singer Helen Cordet, actress Pat Kirkwood, TV presenter Kathy Boyle and others. Elizabeth herself has never commented on the rumors surrounding Philip's alleged cheating. By the way, their marriage lasted for 70 years.

snippet.title: Remember when the Queen got the Giggles with Soldiers in Scotland?
snippet.description:
The Queen visited soldiers while on a visit to Fife, Scotland. She joked about their berets, asking one, “Do you keep it on the whole time, or does it blow off?”

The soldier looked confused and replied: “Erm, it’s supposed to stay on
when we’re stationary, Ma’am…”, and the Queen couldn’t control her laughter! 

#Short

snippet.title: Why did Princess Anne get divorced #queenelizabeth #royalfamily #royal
snippet.description: Princess Anne was the first child of Queen Elizabeth to be allowed not only to tie her life to a commoner, but also to divorce him for marriage to another man of inferior blood. Anna was married to sportsman Mark Phillips for 19 years. In 1977, they had their firstborn son Peter, and four years after that their daughter Zara was born. It was after this that Anna's relationship with her husband began to deteriorate and they decided to live separately. In 1989, The Sun published Princess Anne's love letters, which were obtained illegally. They were written by the Queen's assistant Timothy Laurence. After the publication of the letters, the relationship between Mark and Anna became absolutely unbearable, so the couple decided to separate. However, with an official divorce they were slow. And in 1991, an art teacher from New Zealand named Heather Tonkin said that Captain Phillips is the father of her five-year-old daughter, which was later confirmed by DNA expertise. Princess Anne then filed for divorce. It was finalised on 23 April 1992. In December of the same year, the Princess married Timothy Laurence.

snippet.title: Queen Alexandra - Surviving 50 Years of King Edward VII’s Royal Scandals Documentary
snippet.description:
Queen Alexandra of Denmark was the most beloved woman in the British Empire, but behind her radiant smile lay a life of hidden tragedy and physical disability. This documentary explores the remarkable life of the woman who served as the longest-serving Princess of Wales and eventually Queen Consort to King Edward VII.

While the Edwardian era is often remembered for its lavish parties and the "Marlborough House Set," Alexandra’s private reality was defined by her battle with progressive deafness and the "Alexandra Limp"—a physical disability caused by rheumatic fever that, bizarrely, became a viral fashion trend among the Victorian elite. From her "rags-to-riches" journey as a Danish princess to her complicated marriage to a "Playboy King," we reveal how she navigated his high-profile mistresses (including Alice Keppel) and the strict demands of Queen Victoria.

snippet.title: Prince Andrew & the Epstein Scandal: The Newsnight Interview - BBC News
snippet.description:
In a Newsnight special, Emily Maitlis interviews the Duke of York as he speaks for the first time about his relationship with convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein and allegations which have been made against him over his own conduct.

Please subscribe HERE http://bit.ly/1rbfUog

The Duke of York speaks to Emily Maitlis about his friendship with Jeffrey Epstein and the allegations against him.
In a world exclusive interview, Newsnight’s Emily Maitlis speaks to Prince Andrew, the Duke of York at Buckingham Palace. 
 
For the first time, the Duke addresses in his own words the details of his relationship with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, who took his own life while awaiting trial on sex-trafficking charges.
 
In 2015, Prince Andrew was named in court papers as part of a US civil case against Epstein.
 
The Prince, who is the Queen’s third child, also answers questions about the allegations made against him by one of Epstein’s victims, and discusses the impact of the scandal on the Royal family and his work.

#PrinceAndrew

snippet.title: Royal Scandals and Broken Fairytales - The Truth Behind the British Monarchy
snippet.description:
Step inside the real drama behind the British royal family - from Princess Diana’s fairy tale wedding to scandals, heartbreak, and resilience. Discover the untold stories of royalty.

This in-depth documentary traces the extraordinary journey of the House of Windsor, beginning with Diana’s transformation from a 20-year-old commoner to the world’s most watched princess. Witness the challenges she faced with relentless media scrutiny, her advocacy for charity, and her ultimate break from the royal fairy tale. The video explores a rich tapestry of royal history, revealing past scandals, marriages, and betrayals - from Edward VII’s infamous affairs to the abdication crisis of Edward VIII and the personal struggles of King George VI.

Follow the turbulent relationships of Princess Margaret, Princess Anne, Prince Andrew, and Sarah Ferguson, as the monarchy faces the pressures of modern love and relentless public attention. See how Queen Elizabeth II steered the family through decades of change, keeping tradition alive while navigating family turmoil and public expectation. The documentary also delves into the enduring strength and vulnerability of royal women, the shifting role of the monarchy, and Diana’s enduring legacy as an icon of compassion and feminism.

Whether you’re fascinated by royal history, interested in the truth behind tabloid headlines, or seeking a deeper understanding of the Windsors’ resilience, this film offers a revealing look at the personal and public battles that have shaped the modern British monarchy.

snippet.title: She Was Searching For Love...But Found Only Scandals. #history #royalfamily
snippet.description:
She was one of the "four most beautiful princesses in Europe." Princess Beatrice of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, known to her family as "Baby Bee," was a granddaughter of both Britain's Queen Victoria and Russia's Tsar Alexander II. She was the living embodiment of royal blood.

From an early age, her heart belonged to her first cousin, Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich, the younger brother of Tsar Nicholas II. But this romance was doomed. The Orthodox Church forbade marriages between first cousins. Their love was impossible.

Heartbroken, Beatrice was forced to look for another match. And she found one in a Spanish prince, Infante Alfonso de Orleans y Borbón. But here, too, scandal awaited. Alfonso was the son of an exiled queen, and his family was out of favor with the reigning Spanish king, who was Beatrice's own cousin. King Alfonso XIII forbade the marriage.

But Beatrice and Alfonso, unlike so many others, did not give up. They defied the king. They married secretly in Germany, which caused a scandal. As punishment, the king exiled them from Spain and stripped Alfonso of all his titles. Beatrice, a British princess, was once again an exile.

It was only years later that they were allowed to return to Spain. But their trials were just beginning. With the fall of the Spanish monarchy in 1931, they found themselves in exile once again. And then, the Spanish Civil War erupted.

This is where the darkest chapter of their story begins. Their son, Infante Álvaro, fought for General Franco's Nationalists. But their other son, Alonso, was killed in action, fighting on the same side. It was an unbearable loss.

But even after Franco's victory, their position remained precarious. Franco did not trust members of the royal family. During World War II, Beatrice was arrested on suspicion of being a British spy for the country of her birth.

She survived everything: a forbidden love, a royal scandal, two exiles, a civil war, and the loss of a son. She was a princess who refused to follow the rules, but whose life was a series of losses and disappointments.

snippet.title: Queen Victoria’s secret marriage scandal that was kept hidden by the royal family for 130 years
snippet.description:
In 1872, the Scottish minister Reverend Normal Macleod made a sensational deathbed confession. He told his sister–the only other soul in the room–that he had married Queen Victoria and her Highland Servant John Brown. 

Macleod’s sister kept the secret to herself for another 13 years, and the revelation only became public in 2006. 

Victoria’s husband Prince Albert had appointed the 22-year-old Scotsman to attend especially to the Queen during their visits to Balmoral, and while the two instantly got along, it wasn’t until after Albert’s death in 1861 that their relationship flourished. 

Victoria decreed in 1865 that John Brown would be by her side constantly as her so-called Highland Servant. 

After 1873, John started to wear a plain gold signet ring on the pinkie of his left hand, he was given a house on the Balmoral estate, and the two started to exchange deeply intimate gifts. 

To celebrate the New Year of 1877, Victoria gave John a card with the words, “My lips may give a message better of Christmas love than e’en my letter”, and on a separate undated card to John were the words, “I have loved thee with an everlasting love.” 

So, it’s no surprise that when John died suddenly at just 56 on 27 March 1883 after a mere days-long illness, Victoria was confronted by a sadness only comparable to the loss she felt when Albert died. 

Victoria had John’s hand cast and carved into stone, with his gold signet ring still wrapped around his pinkie, and she started to openly wear John’s mother’s wedding ring–which remains on her finger to this day.
